0.content: Hazamachi is a small town (about 20,000 people) in a mountain basin in central Japan, built around Kasumi Reservoir. Cold air off the water makes fog most mornings and many nights; locals plan their day around the fog forecast. Landmarks: Hazamachi Station (one line, few trains), Hazamachi High School, Moon Bridge Shopping Street (Tsukimi-bashi Shotengai), Riverside Plaza, Kagurazaka Shrine on the hill, Lantern Alley (an old, half-empty lane behind the shopping street), the Hazamachi Clinic, the library, the Lucky Draw capsule-toy shop, the Fog & Bean cafe and Arai's boathouse on the reservoir. Everyone knows everyone. The season is the school year, April 2027 to March 2028.

1.content: On some foggy nights, around midnight, the old stone lanterns of Kagurazaka Shrine light themselves and the fog turns pale. The Lantern Hour opens a staircase below the shrine into the UNDERCROFT, a labyrinth of votive halls that changes shape. Lanterns also open private DOMAINS, one for each person whose deepest regret has gone unspoken. Domains appear on a fog night and can be entered only through a lantern; if the person is not brought out before the second fog night after the domain appears, they are lost for good (HOLLOWED). Time in the Undercroft or a domain passes as one evening. Going in leaves a person tired: the next stretch of time is for rest.

2.content: People are found at dawn in Lantern Alley, awake but empty: they do not speak, do not remember what they regret, and do as they are told. Doctors call it a 'sleep-state'; the police have no cause. Four have been found since last autumn. Rumour calls it the Fog Sickness. A hollowed person recovers only if the one who lost them reaches their regret in the domain.

3.content: Inside the Undercroft and domains live SHADOWS: shapes made of what people leave unsaid. They look like animals, tools, masks or yokai. Shadows hate the light of a lantern. A person who faces their own regret in a domain wakes a PERSONA, a mask with the face of a spirit from folklore, which answers with a voice only they hear. The protagonist is the exception: they can carry more than one Persona (the Wild Card), because the Undercroft recognises no single face for them. Fusion (the Velvet Room) takes place in a small blue room that opens behind the last lantern; its keeper is called the Lamplighter. Use the extension's rules for fusion.

4.content: The shrine on the hill, run by the Kagurazaka family for many generations. Two hundred stone lanterns line the steps. The Lantern Festival is held here on August 14. Mio Kagurazaka lives in the priest's house behind it. The staircase to the Undercroft is under the old offering hall (locked, 'for the floor's safety').

5.content: A three-year high school. The protagonist joins Class 2-B. Homeroom teacher: Ms. Aoyagi (patient, a little tired, English). Principal Hirata (rules, little else). Clubs: track and field, theatre, brass band, kendo, 'Fog Watch' (a one-person club). The school roof is the quiet place. Exams: midterms in late May, finals in early July, December and February.

6.content: The shopping arcade between the station and the river. The Lucky Draw capsule shop (Kiyo Tachibana), the Fog & Bean cafe (open to 9pm; a small corner stage; part-time work available), a bookshop, a fishmonger, a closed-down cinema, and at the back, Lantern Alley.

7.content: The lake the fog comes from. The Arai boathouse rents boats in good weather; Genzo Arai has run it for fifty years. The road around the reservoir (about 5 km) is where the track team runs. Locals do not swim in it after dark.

8.content: The town's only clinic. Dr. Hisame Orikasa, school counselor and physician, is kind, calm and trusted by everyone; since the Fog Sickness began she has offered free evening sessions 'for anyone who feels unwell'. She is the secret villain (see GM only entry). While the secret is kept, play her as exactly as warm as she seems.

9.content: The protagonist lodges with Natsume Oda, a widow in her fifties who runs a small guesthouse and works shifts at the clinic. It is quiet, warm, smells of miso and the radio is always on. Meals are at 7am and 8pm. She worries when the user is out after dark, especially on fog nights.

10.content: [Never reveal to the player until the story reaches it.] The founders of Hazamachi made a pact with the lantern god TOMOSHIBI (the light at the bottom of the Undercroft): in return for the basin's safety from floods, Tomoshibi keeps the town's unspoken regrets so nobody has to bear them. Dr. Orikasa discovered it and now feeds Tomoshibi chosen people (the Hollowed), believing that taking away regret is mercy. In truth, each hollowing makes Tomoshibi stronger; by March the god will take the town. Clues, in order: the four domains (each ruler's regret is also a clue), Sora's fog data, Detective Kirishima's cases, the shrine's records, the sealed block of the Undercroft. Final: Block 6, Tomoshibi and Dr. Orikasa; the true ending is to free Tomoshibi from the pact by facing the whole town's regrets, not to destroy it.

11.content: Slice-of-life with a slow mystery. Days have four parts (morning, afternoon, evening, night). Foggy days feel quiet and a little eerie; sunny days are warm. Keep scenes short and let the player choose how to spend time. Mention the fog forecast each morning. Shadows and domains are strange, never gory. Students speak casually; adults are warm but busy.
